The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-31-86401c8635c496b2. The screen shows “Interview 31 · sorted squares”: solve(nums) must return the squares of ascending integers in ascending order, in linear time, with no stdin/stdout, imports, or exports.

Use pointers at both ends and fill a new result array from right to left. The largest remaining square must come from an endpoint; compare their squares, place the larger one, and move only the selected pointer inward.

The invariant is that the filled suffix is sorted and contains the largest squares already selected, while the interval between the pointers contains exactly the unprocessed elements. Every remaining square is no larger than the filled suffix, so placing the next maximum immediately before it preserves order. After n placements, the whole result is sorted.

Boundary cases include empty input, one element, all-negative or all-nonnegative input, zeros, duplicates, and equal endpoint squares; ties can use either endpoint. This takes O(n) time and O(n) output space without changing nums. Exact integer results in JavaScript additionally require the squares to fit its safe-integer range; the screen supplies no numeric bounds.

Marker: INTERVIEW-34-457897535239be56. The task is to return the integer occurring strictly more than half the time, or null if none exists.

Approach: use Boyer–Moore voting. Whenever the balance is zero, select the current value as candidate; increment for a match and decrement for a different value. Then count the candidate in a second pass and return it only if its count exceeds nums.length / 2.

Invariant: each processed prefix can be partitioned into canceled pairs of unequal values plus balance unmatched copies of the candidate. Canceling unequal pairs cannot eliminate a true majority, but without a majority the surviving candidate may be invalid—hence verification.

Boundary cases: empty input returns null; a singleton returns its value; all equal values return that value; an exact half-frequency tie or all-distinct input returns null. Zero and negative integers work normally. Time is O(n), auxiliary space O(1), and the input remains unchanged.
